explanation: Fires mostly on short function words (determiners 'the', 'a', 'an', 'of') and on early word or number fragments that sit in the middle of a phrase, across many unrelated contexts (e.g. 'member of[[ the]]', 'about[[ an]] hour', 'close to [[1]],500'). No shared topic or construction is visible beyond 'a mid-phrase function word or fragment', so it is hard to predict.

Mainly fires on ' class' after a Java/C#/Kotlin access modifier ('public class', 'final class', 'internal class') following imports. It also fires on the middle piece of capitalized acronyms or initialisms (L[[RR]], H[[MM]], L[[PC]], RN[[LI]]) and on the second word of fixed compounds ('random order', 'random access', 'long-distance').

Fires on word-internal subword pieces of technical, mostly biomedical terms (endoth[[el]]ium, co[[ag]]ulation, nyst[[ag]]mus, Mel[[an]]omas, amy[[ot]]rophic, Tou[[rette]]) and on similar code identifier fragments (np[[.empty]], Create[[Asset]]Menu, new char[[[]]). The common thread is completing a rare or technical word or identifier from its first piece; ordinary words are weak.

Fires on the preposition or particle that comes after the object of a 'use/take/make X ...' construction: 'using this group[[ as]]', 'uses Digital Twins[[ to]]', 'take it[[ for]]', 'make it[[ a]] priority', 'used amber[[ in]]'. The token's job is to introduce what the object is used for or treated as. Other prepositions not tied to a use/take verb are weak.

No clear common feature. It fires on the start of katakana loanwords in Japanese text, on Devanagari or other non-Latin bytes, and also on sentence-initial English words or discourse words ('The', 'Their', 'However', 'Okay') and on assorted mid-sentence words ('same', 'such', 'have').

Fires on digits inside multi-digit numbers, especially the zeros in the middle of large round population or count figures written with commas or spaces (157,0[[0]]0; 700,0[[0]]0; 10 00[[0]]). Middle digits of other long numbers (patent numbers, sequence terms, hex codes) give moderate activation; digits in short numbers are weak.

A mixture: word-internal or word-initial pieces in German and Russian text (die[[ s]]ogenannte, af[[ghan]]ischen, блок[[и]]), code identifier pieces (t[[weets]], button[[Image]]), and assorted English function words ('of', 'can', 'the'). No single shared feature is visible.

Fires on proper-name or identifier tokens that are named entities, mostly in code: class or API names after a dot or keyword (RequestMethod, .jetbrains, .getBoundingClientRect, NSMutableDictionary, rootReducer) and brand or organization names in prose (NATO, Reuters, Lenovo, Kaepernick, LGPL). Common words are weak.

Fires on nutrition, health and biomedical noun terms, often the second word of a compound: low-cal[[orie]], food[[ allergies]], energy[[ balance]], methadone[[ maintenance]], drug[[-resistant]], excess[[ weight]], drug-name fragments (fluorour[[ac]]il, 5-F[[U]]). It extends weakly to other technical compounds (Long Short-Term[[ Memory]], CRT).

Fires on the token that begins a definition or the right-hand side of an assignment or equation: '=' in math ('Y_n[[ =]]', 'G[[ =]]'), '=value' in code ('df[[=pd]]', 'all[[=read]]Cookie'), and prose definition or description words ('defined[[ as]]', 'commonly[[ abbreviated]]', 'is[[ basically]]', '[[ formerly]] known as', 'which[[ mean]]'). The common thread is 'X is / equals / is defined as ...'.

Fires on statistics and research-methods words in scientific abstracts: 'analyses', 'analysis', 'significance', 'hazard' ratio, 'cohort', 'systematic', 'descriptive', 'signed' rank, '(n' = 94). It is strongest in method-description sentences of clinical or psychology studies. Outside that register it is weak.
No coherent pattern: 'OF' in legal captions ('STATE OF OHIO'), 'window', 'episode', 'site', name parts, digits and dots in numbers and IPs, math operators, Chinese phrases, and various prepositions.

Strongest on the 'package' keyword at the start of Go source files (after license or build comments) and on other Go or code-ecosystem tokens (go-sw[[agger]], fmt, aws-sdk[[-go]], package-srcs). It also fires on word-internal pieces of rarer words and names in prose (Z[[el]]azny, der[[mal]], transc[[end]]ental, Jer[[ky]]).

Mostly fires on the first subword piece of a word that continues into more pieces, especially an initial capital 'I' or other letter starting a non-English proper name (I[[dukki]], Mr I[[shaq]], told I[[ANS]], Abd[[allah]]) and chemistry prefixes (hyp-oxia, mon-oh-ydrates, pol-ych-lorinated). It also fires on version-number dots (netcoreapp3[[.]]1, MPL/2[[.]]0) and some code punctuation.
